subject: Locating a Codex CLI / control entry on Windows (read-only search)
method: Read-only lookups: PATH search, npm global package listing, Start Menu and per-user program directories, MSIX package inventory (winget list), and top-level directory-name listing of the user's .codex home. No file contents under the user's .codex home were read; no application was launched.

findings.startMenuAndProgramDirs: No codex-named entries in user or all-users Start Menu programs, nor in per-user LocalAppData Programs

msixInventory.note: Inventory display name and package identity are observations only. Package payload executables and app-server support were not inspected; the desktop label does not exclude bundled Codex functionality or a CLI.

userCodexHome.inspection: Top-level names only; file contents were not read. Existence and filenames do not establish which product created the directory or whether the standalone CLI was used.

conclusion: No Codex CLI entry was identified in the searched PATH, npm global, Start Menu and per-user Programs locations. Inventory reports display name ChatGPT and MSIX identity OpenAI.Codex 26.825.6671.0. The installed package payload was not searched for bundled CLI executables, so no conclusion about that payload or prior CLI use follows. Windows app-server control remains unestablished and all control capabilities remain unknown.

reviewReferences.relevance: Official documentation describes Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app; a desktop display label alone does not rule out Codex functionality.
